intervals.label: LSC operating (research programme grew from the 1985 project)
intervals.note: The LSC's own history page dates the start of the underground research project to 1985 ('A. Morales ... started a project to exploit the underground space ... to house possible low background experiments'). No official page consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives a separate later date for when the present-day LSC consortium formally began operating, so 1985 stands as the earliest sourced start. The interval is marked active because LSC's own site describes the laboratory as operating, not as a separate construction phase.
intervals.quote: In 1985 A. Morales and the Nuclear Physics and Astroparticle Physics Group of the University of Zaragoza started a project to exploit the underground space in the abandoned railway tunnel to house possible low background experiments.

operator_text.quote: a Consortium of the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation, the Aragon Regional Government and the University of Zaragoza.
operator_text.value: A Consortium of the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation, the Aragon Regional Government and the University of Zaragoza

summary.plain: An underground laboratory beneath a mountain in the Spanish Pyrenees, reached through a disused railway tunnel near Canfranc. Its 800 metres of rock shield sensitive experiments searching for dark matter and rare nuclear processes.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory under Mount Tobazo, Canfranc-Estacion, Huesca, Spain, at ~800 m depth, built from the disused Somport railway tunnel; run by a consortium of the Spanish government, the Aragon regional government and the University of Zaragoza; project origins trace to 1985 work by A. Morales's group at Zaragoza.
